tasks.title: Workers and the wave-runner preflight before hand-off
tasks.summary: Factory-level. The coder, tester and grader templates run their role's `bs results check --as <role>` line before hand-off, and wave.md runs `--as gate` with the gate line's flags before `gate run`; the grader fixes shape only, never a verdict; wave.md's gate example carries the envelope flags; the tester's screenshot rule loses its dead fallback; wave.md reads an env-failure classification without a coder bounce or an automatic re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. Put the preflight and the evidence-backed rules into the worker templates and the wave playbook, and document them. (a) .claude/agents/bs-coder.md, bs-tester.md and bs-grader.md: as the last step before returning, run the role's `bs results check <task-id> --as <role>` line the brief gives (coder: `--result --agent --provider --model-tier --worktree --base --artifacts-dir`; tester: `--result --agent --provider --model-tier --plan --artifacts-dir`; grader: `--grader <file> --artifacts-dir`), fix every problem it lists in the worker's own output, re-run it until it exits 0, and quote its final output in the result `notes`. A problem the worker cannot fix in its own output (a flag its brief got wrong, an environment problem) is reported in `notes` as it stands, never worked around. A worker whose brief carries no such line says so in `notes`. bs-grader.md adds: the preflight checks the grader file's shape only; a well-formed fail verdict exits 0 and shows in `verdicts.grader`; the grader fixes shape (where the verdict sits, missing criterion fields, the round number) and never changes a verdict, a criterion's status or its evidence to get a clean preflight. Text identical in the three templates goes in one new `.claude/fragments/handback-preflight.md` with a SHARED region in each; role-specific lines stay in each template. (b) bs-coder.md and bs-tester.md hand-back: run the gate's full command list (the project's full test command, `typecheck`, `typecheck:test` and a whole-repo `biome check .`, never a scoped path) through `bs heavy run`, and report each exit code. Where bs-optimize's heavy-run fragment already says part of this, extend it rather than restate it. (c) bs-tester.md: screenshots are named `<name>-<desktop|mobile>-<light|dark>.png`, the only suffix the gate reads (`SCREENSHOT_RE`); delete the 'or, failing that, in `description`' fallback the code never reads. e2e servers bind port 0 (or a port the runner reports back), and the tester stops only the PIDs it recorded starting. This is a prompt-level rule with no run-time check in v1, an accepted gap that queue-and-gate.md names: a violation surfaces only as a later `tests-failed` block. (d) .claude/skills/bs/wave.md: each worker's brief carries its filled per-role `bs results check` line, with the same `--artifacts-dir` the gate line will carry. Step 7 runs `bs results check <task-id> --as gate` followed by the gate line's own flags, verbatim, before `gate run`; while it exits 1, the wave-runner fixes its own flags or bounces the problem to the worker whose file it names, and does not call `gate run`. A `verdicts.grader` of `fail` or `not-graded` is not a preflight problem and does not stop `gate run`, which records the verdict. Step 7's `gate run` example carries `--agent <role> --provider <name> --model-tier <tier>` as step 5's `results record` example does, and its stage list matches the gate's real order. Step 9: a `gate-outcome` carrying `error_class: execution.env-failure` is logged as `error-logged` with error `execution.env-failure` and the evidence. It raises no finding against the coder, is not bounced to the coder, and the wave-runner does not re-run the gate on its own: whether and when to re-gate stays the epic session's decision, and a second env-classified block for the same task at the same HEAD goes to the operator. Steps 2-10 keep their numbers; dispatch.md is not edited. (e) docs/guide/operator-guide/queue-and-gate.md section 5: document `bs results check` (its modes and the stage set of each, what it never runs, its output and exit codes), the env-failure classification (evidence fields, `SLEEP_GAP_MS`, load as evidence only, the outcome stays blocked) and the port-0 accepted gap. (f) CHANGELOG.md `## Unreleased`: one entry per task of this epic, written from each task's result notes.
acceptance_criteria: bs-coder.md, bs-tester.md and bs-grader.md each tell the worker, before its return line, to run its role's `bs results check --as <role>` line from its brief, fix every problem in its own output, re-run until exit 0, quote the output in `notes`, and report a problem it cannot fix in its own output instead of working around it; test/handbackPreflight.test.ts pins each template and parses each role's example line against usage.ts.

bs-grader.md states that the preflight checks shape only, that a well-formed fail verdict exits 0, and that the grader never changes a verdict, a criterion's status or its evidence to get a clean preflight; the test pins that sentence.

wave.md step 7 runs `bs results check <task-id> --as gate` before `gate run`, with every flag of step 7's `gate run` line; the test parses both step-7 lines and requires the preflight line to carry every flag the gate line carries. Step 7's `gate run` example carries `--agent`, `--provider` and `--model-tier`, as step 5's `results record` example does, and step 7 says a `verdicts.grader` fail or not-graded does not stop `gate run`; the test pins both.
Every per-role brief line in wave.md carries `--artifacts-dir` with the same value as the gate line; the test pins it.

bs-tester.md states the `-<desktop|mobile>-<light|dark>.png` rule and contains no `description` fallback; the test imports `SCREENSHOT_RE` from src/paperwork.ts and checks the stated rule against it. bs-tester.md requires port 0 (or a reported port) for e2e servers and stopping only recorded PIDs, and queue-and-gate.md names this as a prompt-level rule with no run-time check in v1.

bs-coder.md and bs-tester.md name the full test command, `typecheck`, `typecheck:test` and a whole-repo `biome check .`, run through `bs heavy run`, and carry no scoped lint or test example; the test pins it.

wave.md step 9 states the env-failure handling: `error-logged` / `execution.env-failure` with the evidence, no finding, no coder bounce, no automatic gate re-run, the re-gate decision stays with the epic session, and a repeat at the same HEAD goes to the operator; the test pins it.

Every `bs ...` invocation in the changed files parses against usage.ts (test/docCommands.test.ts passes); `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs --check` reports no drift and no unused fragment; wave.md keeps steps 2-10; dispatch.md is unchanged.

queue-and-gate.md section 5 documents `bs results check` (modes, stage sets, what it never runs, output, exit codes), the env-failure classification and the port-0 accepted gap; CHANGELOG.md `## Unreleased` has one entry per task of this epic.

Diff check (AC8), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|flaky|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (a moved line whose value is unchanged, or prose that forbids the thing). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

functional_clauses: Every preflight line in the templates and in wave.md is `bs results check` with `--as` and flags that exist in usage.ts for that mode; no template runs a test command as part of the preflight.
No template or playbook tells a worker to change a verdict, a finding or a test to get a clean preflight.
The env-failure handling never passes a task, never re-runs the gate automatically and never drops a gate stage, grader, judge, review round or verifier.
No rule is stated twice: a rule bs-optimize's heavy-run fragment already carries is referenced or extended, not restated.
Only wave.md, the three templates, the new fragment, queue-and-gate.md, CHANGELOG.md and the new test change.
nonfunctional_clauses: Read factory/specs/active/bs-gate-bounce/epic-spec.md before starting. Do not edit it: it sits outside every task's claims. Put one Progress line for it in the result `notes` (what changed, and anything a later task must know); the epic session copies it in at merge.
TDD: write each new test first, run it and watch it fail for the stated reason, then implement until it passes.

Before hand-back run, in the foreground and in full: `pnpm run build`, root `pnpm run test` (the whole suite, never a scoped file), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test` and `pnpm exec biome check .` (the whole repo, never a scoped path); report each exit code and the tail of each output. Run the full suite through `bs heavy run` (bs-optimize, on main before this epic starts) so it takes the machine's heavy lock.
Also run `bash scripts/check.sh` and read the tail of its output, not only its exit code; name every step it printed as SKIP.

Weaken nothing: add no `.skip`, `.only`, `.todo`, `.fails`, `retry`, quarantine list or flaky marker; raise no `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout`, `timeout_ms`, `waitForLines` default, `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` or any other timeout or deadline; remove, loosen or reorder no existing assertion, gate stage, grader, judge, review round or verifier.

No other project's name, no client code and no absolute home-directory path (`/Users/...`, `/home/...`) in any committed file, test fixture included; fixtures use placeholder paths. Say "dogfood epics" for the factory's own client runs.
Add no runtime or dev dependency.
Do not edit anything under factory/policies/.
Write operator-facing prose in English, plain and short; keep each template's existing structure and headings.
Run `node scripts/sync-shared-fragments.mjs` after editing the fragment, then `--check`, and report both outputs.
